title: Fed Decision in September?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's September 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for September 15-16, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their September meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent U.S. inflation readings staying above the Federal Reserve’s 2 percent target, alongside a stable labor market with August payroll gains of 162,000 and unemployment holding at 4.1 percent, have kept trader odds nearly even between no change and a 25 basis point hike at the September 15-16 FOMC meeting. Official projections from the June SEP showed median expectations for higher policy rates by year-end, while recent speeches from Fed officials have stressed data dependence on incoming inflation prints before the decision. Mixed employment trends earlier in the summer and ongoing uncertainty over energy prices have reinforced the close contest, with any stronger-than-expected CPI or PCE release in the next week likely to shift implied probabilities toward tightening.

title: US Open ATP: Ben Shelton vs Stefanos Tsitsipas
description:
This market refers to the tennis match between Ben Shelton and Stefanos Tsitsipas in the US Open ATP, originally scheduled for September 6, 2026 at 11:00AM ET.

This market will resolve to 'Ben Shelton' if Ben Shelton advances against Stefanos Tsitsipas.

This market will resolve to 'Stefanos Tsitsipas' if Stefanos Tsitsipas advances against Ben Shelton.

If the match is canceled (not played at all), ends in a tie, or a winner has not been determined by September 20, 2026, 11:59 PM ET (14 days after the scheduled start), this market will resolve to 50-50.

If the match begins but is not completed, and one player advances due to the opponent's retirement, default, or disqualification, this market will resolve to the player who advances.

If the match ends in a walkover (player withdraws before the start and the other advances automatically), this market will resolve to 50-50.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the ATP Tour. A consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

This market refers to the tennis match between Ben Shelton and Stefanos Tsitsipas in the US Open ATP, originally scheduled for September 6, 2026 at 11:00AM ET.
This market will resolve to "Over" if the total number of games completed in the first set equals or exceeds 9. Otherwise, it will resolve to "Under." Any first-set tiebreak counts as one (1) game.
If the match is postponed or suspended, this market will remain open until the first set has been completed. A postponement alone will not trigger a 50-50 resolution.
If the match is permanently abandoned before the first set is completed, or if the first set has not been completed by September 20, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve 50-50, unless the outcome has already been unconditionally determined based on completed play. An outcome is considered determined if it would have been guaranteed had the set been played to completion using the minimum number of additional games required. For example, for a line of 9.5, if play stops with the first set at 5-4, completing the set would have required at least 1 additional game, resulting in at least 10 games played, so "Over" would resolve as the winning outcome.
The primary resolution source for this market will be official Grand Slam statistics; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Ben Shelton enters the US Open round of 16 as the clear favorite against Stefanos Tsitsipas, backed by a 36-13 record in 2026, a top-10 ranking, and strong recent hard-court results including multiple deep runs and titles. The American’s explosive left-handed serve and forehand create consistent pressure on Tsitsipas’ one-handed backhand, a stylistic mismatch amplified by Arthur Ashe Stadium’s home crowd. Tsitsipas, ranked 53 after a challenging year, has shown resurgence by upsetting higher seeds like Arthur Fils and Jiri Lehecka to reach this stage for the first time in years while working with coach Patrick Mouratoglou. Shelton leads recent form metrics and holds a significant edge in serve dominance and consistency, though Tsitsipas owns their sole prior meeting from 2023 Cincinnati.

eventMetadata.context_description: Carlos Alcaraz leads the 2026 US Open winner market at 60.5% implied probability as the defending champion returning from a multi-month wrist layoff, with recent straight-sets wins over Tommy Paul and others demonstrating sharp baseline play and serve dominance on hard courts. Jannik Sinner’s pre-tournament withdrawal with a knee injury cleared the top of the draw, elevating Alcaraz while giving Alexander Zverev (21.6%) a cleaner path to the final as the top seed and recent French Open champion with strong hard-court history. American contenders Ben Shelton (9.0%), Frances Tiafoe (4.2%), and Learner Tien (3.2%) have advanced deep into the second week, reflecting solid recent form and home support that has tightened their shares amid an otherwise open field.

eventMetadata.context_description: The Chicago White Sox hold a 74-68 record and lead the AL Central by 2½ games over the Cleveland Guardians, while the Minnesota Twins sit at 68-74 and trail the final wild-card spot by 3½ games. The White Sox enter the rubber match of their series at Rate Field with home-field edge and a stronger overall pitching staff, though they have dropped five of seven. Minnesota counters with Bailey Ober on the mound against a White Sox bullpen game or starter like Bryan Hudson, but key Twins arms including Joe Ryan remain on the injured list. Recent series results show competitive games decided by timely hitting and bullpen work, with playoff positioning adding urgency for both clubs as the regular season winds down.

eventMetadata.context_description: No. 9 Ole Miss enters as the clear favorite against No. 24 Louisville in the neutral-site season opener due to returning star power and quarterback experience. Trinidad Chambliss returns as a Heisman contender after leading the Rebels to a College Football Playoff semifinal in 2025, paired with elite running back Kewan Lacy, while new head coach Pete Golding installs his scheme following Lane Kiffin’s departure. Louisville counters with a stout defense and explosive running back Isaac Brown but faces uncertainty at quarterback with Ohio State transfer Lincoln Kienholz making his first career start. Both teams are largely healthy, with the matchup highlighting Ole Miss’s edge in proven production against Louisville’s portal-fueled roster depth and recent upset pedigree under Jeff Brohm.

title: Will AfD win an absolute majority of seats in Sachsen-Anhalt?
description:
Parliamentary elections to elect the Landtag of Sachsen-Anhalt are scheduled to take place on September 6, 2026.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the party Alternative for Germany (AfD) wins an absolute majority of seats in the state parliament of Sachsen-Anhalt (Landtag) as a result of this election. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If voting in the Sachsen-Anhalt election for the Landtag does not occur or the results are not known definitively by January 31, 2027, this market will resolve to "No".

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named party.

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as published on the official website of the Landtag of Sachsen-Anhalt (https://www.landtag.sachsen-anhalt.de/).

eventMetadata.context_description: **AfD secured the largest share of votes in the September 6, 2026, Sachsen-Anhalt Landtag election but fell short of an absolute majority.** Projections and early results gave the party roughly 44% of the vote and 39 seats in the 83-seat parliament, three short of the 42 needed for a majority. Multiple other parties, including the CDU, SPD, Greens, Left, and BSW, cleared the 5% threshold and took the remaining seats. This outcome aligns with pre-election polling trends showing AfD support in the low-to-mid 40s, insufficient under the current seat distribution to reach a governing majority on its own. The election's high turnout and fragmentation of the remaining vote further reduced the likelihood of the threshold being met, producing the near-certain trader consensus reflected in the 99.8% probability on "No." Late shifts in final certified results or recounts remain the only narrow paths to alteration.

eventMetadata.context_description: Notre Dame enters as a heavy favorite against Wisconsin in their Shamrock Series opener at Lambeau Field, reflecting the Irish's top-five preseason ranking, return of key contributors like quarterback CJ Carr, and strong defensive unit after a 10-2 finish in 2025. Wisconsin, coming off a 4-8 campaign, relies on transfer quarterback Colton Joseph and an offensive line dealing with injuries, including right guard Emerson Mandell sidelined while right tackle Kevin Heywood is expected available. The neutral-site venue offers the Badgers some historical edge from prior Lambeau successes, yet Notre Dame's depth and experience create a significant talent gap in this Week 1 matchup. Trader consensus aligns with the mismatch in roster strength and recent program trajectories.

title: Next French Presidential Election
description:
The next French presidential election is currently expected to be held around April 2027.  This market pertains to the outcome of the next French presidential election, regardless of whether it follows the scheduled end of the current term or is held earlier. 

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

The next French presidential election is currently expected to be held around April 2027.  This market pertains to the outcome of the next French presidential election, regardless of whether it follows the scheduled end of the current term or is held earlier. 

The President of France is elected via a two-round system; a candidate must secure over 50% of the vote to win outright in the first round. If no candidate achieves this, the top two contenders advance to a runoff.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If, for any reason, the results of the election are not known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the French Government, specifically the Ministry of the Interior (https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Marine Le Pen leads trader pricing at 36% amid the Rassemblement National’s consistent first-round strength near 34-36% in September 2026 polls, bolstered by her July candidacy declaration after an appeals court reduced her ineligibility period. Édouard Philippe sits at 29.5% as the strongest center-right option, outpacing Gabriel Attal in head-to-head scenarios and drawing support from Macron-aligned voters, while Jean-Luc Mélenchon holds 12.5% on the fragmented left. A crowded field of declared candidates, the October socialist primary, and limited consolidation among centrists or conservatives keep the race open, with runoff qualification hinging on turnout patterns and late alliances ahead of the April 2027 first round.

title: Brazil Presidential Election
description:
A presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate that wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If the result of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

eventMetadata.context_description: Lula da Silva maintains a lead in trader consensus for Brazil’s October 2026 presidential election due to his position as incumbent with consistent first-round polling around 38–40 percent and a narrow but durable edge in runoff simulations against Flávio Bolsonaro. Recent Datafolha, Quaest, and AtlasIntel surveys from late August and early September show the gap narrowing to within the margin of error in head-to-head matchups, reflecting a polarized electorate and high rejection rates for both frontrunners. Flávio’s candidacy as the Liberal Party nominee, backed by his father Jair Bolsonaro, has been hampered by prior scandals involving banker Daniel Vorcaro, limited coalition support, and internal family tensions, though he remains the clear second choice at roughly 33–35 percent in first-round tests. Minor candidates such as Augusto Cury have gained from media exposure but trail far behind. The race’s closeness aligns with the current implied probabilities ahead of the October 4 first round and potential October 25 runoff.
